Bottom leaves on plants were turning brown particularly on tomatoes and cucumbers.  Multiple pesticides sprays with various chemistries didn't seen to knock them down. How I cut an onion.
Cut the growth ends off.
Make a slit through the first layer cut to cut with the grain, use that to peel the first layer off.
Cut onion in 1/2 the same way as slice to peel.
Lay 1/2 cut side down and make about 1/8" slices the same way as it was cut in 1/2. Hold it all together while doing this. I use this cut for cheesesteaks for example.
If you want them diced small for garnish for example, while the onion is still held together on the board, spin it and make additional cuts 1/8" apart  in the other direction.

New Year's Chicken Tortillas🌮
Ingredients:

* 1 Kg chicken fillets
* 2-3 sweet peppers
* 1 Red onion
* 1 Lime
* 6 tbs of fajita seasoning (or use feeling)
* 100g Lettuce
* Salsa
* Creme fraiche
* Tortilla wraps

Directions:

1. Cut the chicken into thin strips
2. Season the chicken with fajita seasoning and lime juice ( I use my homemade seasoning)
3. Let marinade for 1 hr
4. Cut the sweet peppers and red onion into thin slices
5. Fry the marinated chicken and set aside once done
6. In the same pan, add the vegetables, add more fajita seasoning and sautee
7. Warm tortilla wraps and add creme fraiche, salsa, fajita, cheese, lettuce and lime juice.

I wouldn't sauté the powders, they're likely to burn if sautéed alone. Just add them directly to your water and/or stock and/or broth (whatever cooking liquid you're using). You can also pre-chop a small amount of onions to keep in the fridge for the week, pre-chop a bunch of onions and freeze them, or even buy some frozen chopped onions. I've never bought the frozen chopped onions before myself, but I've heard that they hold up pretty well. For onions you chop yourself and freeze, try to freeze them in a relatively even layer to avoid overly large frozen clumps, or freeze them in individual portions.

Other things you can use to add flavour to your rice:

* Whole cumin seeds
   * You can either add them directly to your cooking liquid or sauté in some oil (you'll get more flavour that way) as whole spice aren't going to burn the same way ground ones would
* You can also freeze some diced carrots and/or celery the same way as the onions and sauté those in your pot before adding the rice.
* Stir in some lemon juice and/or lemon zest to the rice after cooking it.
   * You can use the same principle with limes
   * If you happen to have some on hand, stirring in some fresh parsley and/or cilantro works well with the lemons or lime. You can just tear some or it up if you don't want to chop.

For clarity: you cut store bought onions in half and replanted? 

If so, those onions were now in their "2nd year" of growth, and all they do in that 2nd year is produce flowers for seeds. You can collect the seeds and plant them early next year for an onion harvest around June if you'd like. 

You'll want to buy and plant onion sets (they look like bags of miniature onions) or onion seeds if you want an onion harvest.

Iceberg is notoriously flavorless. It’s mostly good as a filler in sandwiches and the like, where they add more texture than flavor.

For salads, try romaine. It’s more popular. Other greens like watercress and arugula have a peppery flavor that can work in some recipes. For an Asian salad dressing, you might also try Napa cabbage.

I find onion seeds really easy to germinate. You could save yourself some money going that route. The goal is to get long stems in winter so in spring the plant can get more sun and grow bigger bulbs. When the bulbs start forming, dig out the dirt touching the bulb (leaving the roots covered) this helps the bulbs grow bigger as well. Use fertiliser to help grow the large green stems but stop when the bulbs are forming and be careful not to over water. You can't really overwater them until they start forming bulbs. I wait for my stems to brown and fall over before I harvest them. When I do, I leave the onions on top of the soil I dug them from in direct sunlight for a week to cure (bring inside if consitent rain is around, small showers are fine) Then I braid them the dead stems and hang them up for long term storage. Happy growing!
